To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein oxidation of an 800-10000 year old hair sample was comparable to recent hair samples but glycoxidation was significantly higher in the ancient specimen.
the oxidation of protein and glycoxidative modification of protein were different in the Alaskan child and the coptic specimen.
Ice preserved the protein of an Alaskan mummy for 800-1,000 years without significant oxidation of the protein but with high glycoxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of chemical reactions of biological molecules, in this case hair proteins, over long periods of time.
the chemical stability of proteins and peptides in the past, present and future.
the chemical changes of organic matter in the course of time, which are of interest to archaeologists and palaeochemicists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxidation of proteins and the oxidation of sugars are two independent processes, and that they do not necessarily go together.
the Alaskan hair sample was better preserved than the coptic hair samples.
the oxidation of hair proteins is a complex reaction, influenced by several factors, including the environment and the age of the sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Alaskan child was preserved by ice but not the coptic mummies by hot dry sand.
the Alaskan child died of a cold death and that the copt was killed by heat and dehydration.
the oxidation of proteins in hair is mainly influenced by the environment and not by the age of a sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the preservation of proteins in ice is not necessarily the result of low temperature but of low water activity.
protein oxidation can be used as a biomarker to determine preservation mechanisms and to assess the quality of ancient organic matter.
protein oxidation and glycoxodation are not only a function of time but also of the environmental conditions.
